rationale: Reclassification and deeming integrate the technology into inherited carriage law without yet producing mature liability, infrastructure or international layers.

regime_label: 1926 · International Convention relative to Motor Traffic
rationale: Approved type/vehicle examination, driver authorisation and international certificate recognition are institutionalised, while liability and infrastructure remain less converged.
caveat: The liability score reflects the UK/European motor-risk environment rather than obligations created by the 1926 Convention itself.

regime_label: 2018 · EU type-approval baseline + Vienna/WP.29 bridge architecture
rationale: EU law can accommodate new vehicle technologies through type-approval exception/equivalence mechanisms, but full-ADS operational and actor layers remain largely national or inherited.
caveat: 2018 is used as an analytical baseline; Regulation 2018/858 applied later and the score reflects the emerging architecture rather than one single commencement date.

regime_label: 2022 · EU ADS type approval + Vienna Convention Article 34bis
rationale: Dedicated ADS type-approval requirements reach N3 while Article 34bis bridges the driver requirement only where both technical rules and domestic operating law are satisfied; operation and actor allocation therefore remain less normalised.
caveat: Article 34bis entered into force on 14 July 2022; it does not designate the ADS as the legal driver and does not create uniform domestic operational law.

regime_label: 2026 · Consolidated EU ADS type approval + new UNECE ADS Regulation/GTR
bridge: Dedicated technical harmonisation + persistent operational bridges
rationale: Technical and international ADS regulation is comparatively mature, including the June 2026 UNECE ADS instruments, while road operation, actor allocation and infrastructure remain more fragmented. EU 2026/481 moves automated parking toward unlimited-series market access.
caveat: Technical approval is coded N3 overall because N4-like unlimited-series treatment currently applies to a narrower automated-parking sublayer, not to all ADS deployment.

caveat: Scores distinguish enacted legal architecture from operational commencement; the principal authorisation scheme was not yet fully deployable in 2024.

regime_label: 2026 · Pre-full-implementation phase: passenger permits + draft safety principles
rationale: Actor and responsibility architecture is already dedicated, but the full authorisation regime is planned for 2027; 2026 passenger-service permits and trialling provide conditional operational pathways while the Statement of Safety Principles is still being finalised.
caveat: Automated passenger services are more mature than the general authorisation layer; the row codes the overall GB regime rather than the most advanced sub-use-case.
